reason: The developing red cells are making proteins, and haemoglobin's building materials appear to be their next ingredient for carrying oxygen.
expectation: The cells will make haemoglobin as they develop.

effect: The developing cells made haemoglobin and matured into red blood cells without nuclei. I can now assemble the fluid part of the sample.
reaction: The change from nucleated cells to mature discs was interesting.
reason: Plasma water and solutes look like the two parts of the blood's fluid component.
expectation: They will make plasma for the blood sample.

effect: Water and solutes made plasma, so the fluid and red cells are ready to be brought together.
reaction: The plasma's straw-yellow appearance was unexpected.
reason: Red blood cells in plasma should form the basis of a blood sample that can carry oxygen.
expectation: The red blood cells will join the plasma in a blood sample.

effect: Red cells could not join plasma yet; the automatic combination showed haemoglobin binding and releasing oxygen. I will try adding the oxygen-bearing cells to plasma.
reaction: I was surprised oxygen had to be added before the cells could join the plasma.
reason: The oxygen-bearing red cells and plasma look like the next parts of the blood sample, though the earlier attempt showed the order matters.
expectation: The oxygen-bearing cells will join the plasma.

effect: The oxygen-bearing red cells are now suspended in plasma; the sample still lacks white cells and platelets.
reaction: The partial sample makes the missing components clear.
reason: White cells and platelets are the remaining components shown as absent from the sample.
expectation: They will complete the blood sample.

effect: Adding white cells and platelets completed the blood sample and the chapter goal. The result distinguishes plasma carrying dissolved materials from red cells carrying much of the oxygen.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate components together in the finished sample.

mostWorthwhile.text: The oxygen combination was most worthwhile: it showed that haemoglobin can both bind and release oxygen, connecting the red cells to their carrying job.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making plasma was straightforward but less interesting than seeing how oxygen is carried.

surprise.text: I was surprised that mature red blood cells had no nuclei, and that the game required oxygen to be added before the red cells could join plasma.

arbitrary.text: Requiring oxygen before combining red cells with plasma felt like an unexplained ordering rule; I had expected the cells to join the plasma first.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter to see how circulation brings oxygen carriers close to body cells, though I hope the required order of combinations is clearer.
